scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): concedes that poor schooling can restrain the mind, then argues good education frees it; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: People sometimes blame schools for making students dull and obedient.
Some people argue that formal education tends to restrain our minds and spirits rather than set them free.
I agree that poor schooling can restrain us, but I believe good education frees the mind far more than it limits it.
First, it is true that formal education can sometimes restrain the mind.
Schools that demand only memorising and obedience can dull a student's natural curiosity.
For example, a rigid classroom may punish the very questions that real thinking requires.
This shows that education done badly can narrow the mind instead of opening it.
Forcing every student through the same fixed path can leave little room for imagination.
Some schooling really does train people to follow rather than to think.
To this extent, the statement points to a real danger.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why good education frees the mind

sentences.text: Second, however, good education frees the mind far more than it restrains it.
By teaching us to read, reason, and question, education gives us the tools of free thought.
Consider a student who, through learning, can suddenly understand and judge the wider world.
Such growth shows that knowledge releases people from ignorance and narrow assumptions.
Education also opens doors to choices and freedoms a person would never have had otherwise.
The fault lies not in education itself but only in education done poorly.
Real education, then, sets the mind free rather than chaining it.
In conclusion, badly run education can indeed restrain the mind and spirit.
But good education frees us far more, giving us the power to think for ourselves.
Education limits us only when it is done poorly, and frees us when it is done well.
